newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga gives extra rebate for Penang outage.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga gives extra rebate for Penang outage.

text.p: State-controlled utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd will pay consumers in northern Penang island an extra 10 percent rebate for a June 1995 blackout, Minister of Posts, Energy and Telecommunications Leo Moggie said on Wednesday.
The 10 percent comes on top of an earlier 10 percent rebate announced by the government to compensate for a August 3, 1996 nationwide blackout.
The added rebate would provide Penang island consumers a total of 20 percent in rebates.
"They (consumers) will be paid a total of 20 percent as goodwill in recognition of inconveniences they suffered in the blackout," Moggie said at a news conference.

Earlier this month, the government announced Tenaga would give consumers affected by the peninsula-wide August 3, 1996 blackout a five percent rebate in their December 1996 bills, and another five percent in their January 1997 bills.
Penang island consumers would receive a 10 percent rebate in December followed by another 10 percent rebate in January.
Moggie had said the earlier rebates would cost Tenaga 70 million ringgit.
The additional rebates covering Penang island consumers will cost the utility four million ringgit, Moggie said on Wednesday.

Tenaga's extra rebate for Penang island follows a request by the state government for compensation following a crippling 10-day blackout in June last year. Penang is the hub of the nation's electronic industry.
